messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — KV cache memory growth detected in paged-blockmgr (us-west-2). Continuous-batching rate jumped ~8x; block metadata counts rising rapidly. Auto-escalation triggered.

maya: seeing the same in dashboards — mem heap for blockmgr worker nodes climbing, evictions not keeping up. Paging I/O saturating disks on two hosts.

axel: paging spike correlates with a recent rolling change to batcher v2 (deployed ~1h ago). That change changed `max_continuous_batch_size` default to 2048. Reverting reduces throughput but should cap growth.

sam: confirmed — can we flip the config to 256 as a hotfix? That was our previous safe default.

maya: +1 to rollback. Also want to disable prefetch on those hosts to reduce metadata churn: `kv.blockmgr.prefetch.enabled=false`.

axel: pushing a canary rollback to the us-west pool now. Command:```sh
# rollback batcher v2 to previous config
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart ds/blockmgr-us-west --overwrite=true
redwoodctl config set --scope=pool:us-west kv.batch.max_continuous_batch_size=256
redwoodctl config set --scope=pool:us-west kv.blockmgr.prefetch.enabled=false
```

incident-bot: action logged by axel at 1715554350. PagerDuty: acknowledged.

eve: CS note — two enterprise customers showing >=5% 4xxs and request timeouts (latency > 12s). I've opened a priority ticket and started customer pings.

jordana: metrics: blockmgr metadata_count on host i-0a12 jumped 3.1M -> 18.9M in 30m. Eviction queue depth sat at 98% for 12 minutes. That's the blackhole pattern — new metadata keeps being created faster than eviction.

maya: also seeing many small blocks (block_size=16kb) churn. We historically tuned to 64kb. I think the batcher change caused more fragment allocation. Suggest temporary block_size increase and a conservative eviction multiplier.

axel: applying block_size bump to 64k (hotpatch) on canary hosts:```json
{"kv.blockmgr.block_size":"65536","kv.blockmgr.eviction_multiplier":"1.5"}
```

sam: rolling to remaining hosts after canary looks stable for 4 minutes. Observability: reduce sampling rate to 10% to lower write pressure.

incident-bot: automatic throttle applied: per-queue sampling reduced.

maya: after rollback + block_size bump, eviction queue depth dropped to ~40% and metadata growth rate flattened. Disk I/O also fell ~60%. Latency for affected flows trending back within SLO.

eve: customers updated: two impacted tenants see degraded perf for ~42 minutes, now improving. CS has asked for incident summary and ETA on full remediation.

jordana: root cause notes — batcher v2 default changed to large continuous batch size without blockmgr-aware backpressure. That allowed pathological write amplification: many tiny metadata writes + prefetch amplifying. Combined with a block_size mismatch, we saturated eviction.

axel: next steps: 1) revert batcher default in mainline; 2) add a safety cap in blockmgr to refuse metadata growth > X/min per host; 3) add integration test for batcher+blockmgr interplay. I'll open PRs and link them here.

maya: handoff for next oncall (sam) — keep an eye on metadata_count and eviction_queue. If metadata_count > 20M on any host, execute emergency drain: `redwoodctl cache drain --target=host --grace=60s` and roll back traffic from region.

sam: taking handoff. I've got the runbook open and watcher alerts set. Will coordinate with infra to pre-warm extra hosts if needed.

eve: CS will send incident notification with timeline and mitigation steps. I'll attach logs and affected tenant list.

axel: PRs: 1) rollback default -> https://git.internal/r/infra/1234 (in review), 2) blockmgr reject-threshold -> https://git.internal/r/infra/1235 (draft). Moving to high priority.

maya: retrospective items: add canary of batcher config changes that exercise blockmgr under medium load; add metrics for metadata-write/s creation ratio; ensure our deploy alerts include metadata growth deltas.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE (1715554987): status=mitigated (partial), severity=P1 -> customer impact reduced, monitoring in progress.

sam: I'll run an expedited traffic replay against a staging cluster with the new safety cap to validate. If green, we can ship blockmgr guard next patch.

eve: thanks team — CS will keep the customers updated. Will document impact window and follow up on postmortem. :thumbsup:

maya: resolving this thread for now. Leave notes in the incident tracker and assign postmortem.
